headlines.description: Caltrans is working to protect several Bay Area roadways from potential flooding ahead of next week’s storms and king tides. At about 7 a.m. Friday, Caltrans closed the far-right westbound carpool lane at the Bay Bridge toll plaza so crews could get to work on installing a temporary flood protection system known as a Tiger Dam. The water-filled barrier will stretch about a half-mile from Radio Beach to the metering lights. Caltrans said the barrier uses the weight of the water to anchor itself to the ground, helping to block floodwaters and absorb the impact of waves during king tides. Caltrans plans to monitor the barrier for 10 days. “Our top priority is safety, and what we’re doing is taking proactive measures to make sure that Bay Area residents remain safe,” Caltrans spokesperson Pedro Quintana said. The far-right lane is expected to reopen Monday. All other lanes at the Bay Bridge toll plaza remain open. But if water levels rise higher than expected, additional lane closures are possible. This year’s king tides could be more extreme than usual, and they arrive next week. Elena Givental, an environmental studies professor at California State University, East Bay, said king tides are expected to be at least two feet higher than normal, putting low-lying areas at risk of repeated flooding. “Due to this combination of very active El Niño, Kelvin waves that are part of the El Niño process, and king tides that are kind of normal thing but now are enhanced, we should expect this winter to have this kind of recurrent flooding,” she said. Oakland 18 hours ago Bay Bridge Nov 19 Caltrans also announced a larger closure in Oakland. Starting Sunday at 8 p.m., Caltrans will close the Posey Tube, which connects Oakland and Alameda, until Friday at 5 p.m., the day after Thanksgiving. Caltrans said the Posey Tube has never flooded, but the closure is a precaution ahead of king tides. The Webster Tube will remain open. Caltrans said the Posey Tube is closing because it is closer to the shoreline. “It’s going to make traffic ten times worse. It’s going to be a cluster,” Alameda resident Iwalani Seuser-Smith said. “The other way to Oakland is like an extra 15-20 minutes. I use it every day for work,” Berkeley resident Erik Bonilla said, expressing concern about how many people will be affected. In the North Bay, Caltrans has moved concrete barriers and restriped Highway 37 to prevent flooding during winter storms. Both directions of Highway 37 were shut down between Sears Point and Mare Island in Vallejo. The westbound lanes were expected to reopen first, with eastbound lanes expected to reopen by 6 a.m. Friday.
headlines.source: Damian J. Troise and Alex Veiga | The Associated Press
